title: Ben’s school bag
passage:
Ben packs his school bag on Sunday night. He puts in two pencils, a blue pen, a ruler and his maths book.

He also packs a red water bottle and an apple. His sports shoes go in a different bag, because he has PE on Monday. He leaves his phone on the kitchen table.

In the morning, he adds a cheese sandwich.
option5: Ben puts his phone in his bag.
option7: Ben adds a ham sandwich in the morning.
explanation: Ben packs two pencils, not three. His phone stays on the kitchen table. He packs an apple, and the sandwich is cheese.

title: The Saturday market
passage:
The market opens at eight o’clock on Saturday. There are twelve stalls.

Anna’s stall sells bread and cakes. Next to her, Tom sells fruit: apples, pears and oranges. The flower stall is near the door.

A coffee costs two pounds. The market closes at one o’clock, and the car park is free until two.
option3: The market closes at one o’clock.
option4: The car park is free until two.
option5: The market opens at nine o’clock.
option8: The flower stall is next to Tom.
explanation: The market opens at eight, Anna sells bread and cakes, a coffee is two pounds, and the flower stall is near the door (Anna is next to Tom).

title: Rules for the science room
passage:
Before the lesson starts, leave your bag on the shelf by the window, not on the floor. Tie back long hair and put on safety glasses before you touch any equipment.

Do not eat or drink in the room, not even water. If you break something, tell the teacher at once. Do not try to clean up broken glass yourself.

At the end of the lesson, wash your hands with soap, put the stools under the benches and check that the gas taps are off. The last group to finish wipes the benches.
option1: Bags go on the shelf by the window.
option2: Students must not drink water in the room.
option3: If something breaks, students tell the teacher at once.
option4: The last group to finish wipes the benches.
option5: Students may clean up broken glass if they are careful.
option6: Safety glasses go on after you touch the equipment.
option7: Stools go on top of the benches at the end.
option8: Students wash their hands at the start of the lesson.
explanation: Broken glass is for the teacher to clear up. Safety glasses go on before you touch anything, the stools go under the benches, and hand-washing is at the end of the lesson.

title: A day trip to the coast
passage:
The coach leaves the school gates at 7.30 and stops once, at a service station, for twenty minutes. We arrive in Whitby at about 10.15.

In the morning, groups visit the abbey and climb the 199 steps. Lunch is at 12.30 on the beach. Bring a packed lunch, as there is no time to buy food.

In the afternoon, there is a boat trip around the harbour, which lasts forty-five minutes. The coach leaves Whitby at 3.45 and should be back at school by 6.30. Bring a waterproof coat and £5 for the boat.
option1: The coach stops once on the way there.
option3: The boat trip lasts forty-five minutes.
option5: Lunch is bought at a café in Whitby.
option7: The stop at the service station lasts half an hour.
explanation: Students bring a packed lunch because there is no time to buy food. The coach leaves Whitby at 3.45, and the service station stop is twenty minutes.

title: New library rules
passage:
From 1 March, the town library is changing its opening times and rules. It will open from 9 a.m. to 7 p.m. on weekdays, but close at 4 p.m. on Saturdays, and it will no longer open on Sundays.

Members can now borrow twelve books instead of eight, but DVDs are limited to three at a time and must be returned within a week. Late returns will cost 20p a day for books and 50p a day for DVDs.

The study room upstairs must be booked online, for no more than two hours, and the printers will move from the ground floor to the first floor. Children under eight must be with an adult at all times.
option1: The library will close at 4 p.m. on Saturdays.
option3: DVDs must be returned within a week.
option4: A late DVD costs 50p a day.
option5: The library will open on Sunday mornings.
option6: The study room can be booked for up to three hours.
option7: The printers are moving to the ground floor.
option8: Children under ten must be with an adult.
explanation: The library will no longer open on Sundays. The study room can be booked for two hours at most, the printers are moving up to the first floor, and the age for needing an adult is under eight.

title: The lost rucksack
passage:
Freya lost her rucksack on the number 14 bus on Tuesday afternoon. It is dark green, with a broken zip on the front pocket and a small badge of a fox.

Inside, there was a grey hoodie, a pencil case with her initials (F.R.) on it, a library book called The Silent Coast, a pair of black headphones and a purse with about £8 in coins, but no cards.

Her bus pass was not in the bag: she had it in her coat. She got off at the stop outside the hospital at about 4.20.
option1: The rucksack has a badge of a fox.
option2: The library book is called The Silent Coast.
option3: Freya’s bus pass was in her coat.
option4: The purse had about £18 in it.
option5: Freya lost the bag on the number 41 bus.
option6: The zip on the main pocket was broken.
option7: She got off outside the station.
explanation: The purse had about £8, the bus was the number 14, the broken zip is on the front pocket, and she got off outside the hospital.

title: Climate and Cities: the programme
passage:
The one-day Climate and Cities conference begins with registration from 8.45 in the main hall. The opening talk, by Dr Amira Haddad, starts at 9.30 and looks at heat in city centres.

At 10.45, delegates choose one of three workshops: green roofs (Room 2), cycling networks (Room 5) or flood planning (the library). Lunch is served at 12.15 in the café; vegetarian and vegan meals must be ordered in advance.

The afternoon panel, “Who pays for cooler cities?”, runs from 1.30 to 3.00 and includes the deputy mayor. The poster session closes the day at 3.30, and posters must be taken down by 5 p.m.
option2: The flood planning workshop is in the library.
option3: Vegan meals must be ordered in advance.
option4: The deputy mayor takes part in the afternoon panel.
option5: Dr Haddad’s talk is about flooding in city centres.
option6: The cycling workshop is in Room 2.
option8: Posters may stay up until 6 p.m.
explanation: Dr Haddad’s talk is about heat, not flooding. Room 2 is green roofs (cycling is in Room 5), the panel ends at 3.00 (3.30 is the poster session), and posters come down by 5 p.m.

title: The flat-share agreement
passage:
The four flatmates have agreed the following. The rent of £2,240 a month is split by room size: Jo pays £620, Sam and Priya pay £560 each, and Kit, who has the smallest room, pays £500. Bills are shared equally and paid on the 3rd of each month.

Each person cleans the kitchen for one week at a time, in the order Priya, Kit, Jo, Sam. Guests may stay for up to three nights in a row, but the others must be told a day before.

The living room is quiet after 11 p.m. on weekdays and after midnight at weekends. Anyone who breaks a shared item replaces it within a fortnight.
option2: Bills are paid on the 3rd of the month.
option3: Kit cleans the kitchen after Priya.
option4: Guests can stay for three nights in a row.
option5: Jo and Sam pay the same rent.
option6: Bills are split by room size.
option7: The living room is quiet after 11 p.m. at weekends.
option8: A broken item must be replaced within a month.
explanation: Sam pays the same as Priya, not Jo. The rent is split by room size, but the bills are shared equally. Weekends are quiet from midnight, and a broken item is replaced within a fortnight.

title: A year of acquisitions
passage:
In the past year, the museum acquired 37 objects, nine more than the year before. Of these, 22 were donations, eleven were purchases and four came on long-term loan.

The most expensive purchase, a seventeenth-century Dutch map, cost £48,000, two thirds of which was covered by a heritage grant. The textile collection grew the most, with fourteen additions, while no new ceramics were accepted because of a shortage of storage space.

Two donations were declined: a painting whose ownership history could not be verified, and a set of letters thought better suited to the county archive. Conservation work on the map will delay its display until the spring.
option1: The museum acquired more objects than the year before.
option2: Four objects came on long-term loan.
option3: A grant paid for most of the map.
option4: No ceramics were added this year.
option6: The textile collection gained eleven objects.
option7: The letters were declined because their ownership was uncertain.
option8: The map is already on display.
explanation: Twenty-two objects were donated (eleven were bought). Textiles gained fourteen. It was the painting whose ownership history was uncertain; the letters went to the county archive. The map goes on display in the spring.

title: Changes to the exam timetable
passage:
Following a clash with the regional sports finals, the following changes have been made. The History paper moves from Monday 9 June to Wednesday 11 June, still starting at 9 a.m. Geography Paper 2, previously on the Wednesday afternoon, therefore moves to Thursday 12 June at 1.30 p.m.

Students sitting both Spanish and French should note that the Spanish listening test now begins thirty minutes earlier, at 8.30, to allow a gap before the French oral.

Candidates with extra time will sit in the drama studio rather than the sports hall, which is unavailable all week. The deadline for withdrawing from an exam without a fee remains Friday 30 May.
option1: The History paper still starts at 9 a.m.
option2: Geography Paper 2 is now on a Thursday afternoon.
option3: The Spanish listening test now starts at 8.30.
option4: Candidates with extra time will sit in the sports hall.
option5: The History paper moves to Tuesday 10 June.
option6: There is now a fee for withdrawing before 30 May.
option7: The French oral now starts thirty minutes earlier.
explanation: Extra-time candidates move to the drama studio because the sports hall is unavailable. History moves to Wednesday 11 June, withdrawing before 30 May is still free, and it is the Spanish listening test that moves earlier.
